scope: Every mutable fact used by an in-scope Phase 1 allow decision; this is a contract inventory, not a claim that PostgreSQL serialization has been implemented.

serialization.protected_command: Acquire a shared lock on the actor/tenant authority aggregate, read current dependency values, authorize, and commit protected mutation while holding that lock.
serialization.authority_change: Acquire an exclusive lock on the same actor/tenant authority aggregate before changing a dependency; record the new aggregate version in the same transaction.
serialization.retry: Bounded serialization/deadlock retry reuses the same logical command ID.
serialization.proof_owner: WP2.4 PostgreSQL barrier tests; WP0 defines the complete dependency set and expected serial outcomes.

dependencies.fact: Actor is an active identity with membership in the command tenant.
Actor has an explicit role assignment granting the canonical action.
dependencies.scope: tenant assignment plus global role catalogue
dependencies.serialization_target: actor/tenant aggregate for assignment changes; role definitions are frozen during Phase 1 and any future change must version the global policy catalogue and invalidate affected aggregate versions

dependencies.fact: Any office/appointment required by the action is current, in scope, and supported by the accepted source status.
Actor holds the required active capacity for the target organization and command.
Every delegation link in the actor-to-scope chain is active, unexpired, and in the target cohort/organization.
dependencies.serialization_target: affected delegate actor/tenant authority aggregate; each parent/delegator change also advances affected delegate aggregates before commit

dependencies.fact: The target organization/cohort belongs to the authorized tenant and is within the actor's assigned scope.
dependencies.serialization_target: affected actor/tenant authority aggregate; organization reparenting is a privileged serialized operation

dependencies.fact: Person identity/conflict attributes relevant to a protected action are current and not superseded by a contradictory accepted fact.
mutation_paths: consent withdrawal where it changes permitted processing
dependencies.scope: tenant via person and parent aggregate
dependencies.serialization_target: affected person/tenant authority aggregate; no person data may be added to an authority token or event

dependencies.fact: Action rules, scope policy, approval requirements, and relevant configuration are the version evaluated by the command.
dependencies.serialization_target: tenant/actor aggregate version for tenant policy; global policy catalogue version is frozen in Phase 1 or included in every affected decision snapshot and invalidates authorization when changed

required_invariants: Every allow rule references one or more dependency IDs above; no dependency is silently treated as immutable.
Every mutation path that can change an allow decision participates in the same serialization protocol or is explicitly frozen/versioned.
A command linearized before revocation may commit before it; a command linearized after revocation commit is denied.
No protected mutation commits using an unlocked stale dependency snapshot.
History rows are append-only; current revocation changes future authority and never rewrites historical findings.
